note: Dublin ideas expansion for Ted's 2026-07-28 → 2026-08-12 visit. Trad sessions + daily tours/attractions are modeled as single rows spanning the window (start=first day at real session time, end=Aug 12) so they surface in the ideas 'anyday' bucket every day — same pattern as the existing Dublin Literary Pub Crawl row. One-off gigs/matches/clubnights are per-date rows. Every URL curl-verified 200 on 2026-07-27; Hughes's pub (Chancery St) was dropped because it closed in June 2019.

events.title: Trad Sessions at The Cobblestone
events.blurb: Dublin's most respected session pub — 'a drinking pub with a music problem'. Trad sessions every day: Mon from 6:30pm, Tue–Thu from 4:30pm, Fri from 2pm, weekends from 2:30pm. Under-18s welcome until 9pm.

events.title: Live Trad at O'Donoghue's
events.blurb: The Merrion Row institution where The Dubliners got their start. Live traditional music every night — from about 8pm weeknights, earlier at weekends — with no cover charge.

events.title: Nightly Music at The Brazen Head
events.blurb: Ireland's oldest pub (a hostelry since 1198) has live traditional music every night from 9pm, plus a Sunday afternoon session — worth arriving early to snag a seat in the courtyard.

events.title: Trad Sessions at Devitts of Camden Street
events.blurb: Seven nights of live music on Camden Street: sessions from 6:30pm Mon–Thu, 7:30pm Fri–Sat, and a famous open trad session from 2pm on Sundays where visiting players are welcome to join in.

events.title: Live Trad Daily at Darkey Kelly's
events.blurb: Named for the infamous 18th-century madam of Fishamble Street, this Christchurch pub runs live music every single day — trad sessions most evenings from 7:30pm, with extra afternoon sets at weekends.

events.title: Trad at The Piper's Corner
events.blurb: Musician-owned Marlborough Street bar with a focus on the uilleann pipes — serious nightly sessions from around 9pm where the music, not the chatter, is the point. A locals' favourite over the Temple Bar tourist spots.

events.title: Live Music All Day at The Temple Bar
events.blurb: The famous red pub itself: live Irish music seven days a week from early afternoon until close, no cover charge. Unashamedly touristy, undeniably fun — and the kids can come along during the day.

events.title: Otto Aday
events.blurb: Intimate Wednesday-night set in Whelan's smallest room from rising songwriter Otto Aday.

events.title: Glass Gallery
events.blurb: Upstairs midweek show at Whelan's from alt-pop project Glass Gallery.

events.title: Leon Stax Equation
events.blurb: Funk and soul on Whelan's main stage from the Leon Stax Equation.

events.title: Joshua Ray Walker
events.blurb: Texas country-and-western songwriter with a devastating voice plays an up-close Dublin club show.

events.title: Human – A Tribute to The Killers
events.blurb: Bank-holiday Sunday singalong: The Killers' catalogue front to back from tribute act Human.

events.title: Brendan Hickey
events.blurb: Singer-songwriter Brendan Hickey headlines the snug Little Whelan's room.

events.title: Ryan Carrick
events.blurb: Emerging Irish songwriter Ryan Carrick plays Little Whelan's as the Trad & Folk Festival kicks off next door.

events.title: Cloudbusting – The Music of Kate Bush
events.blurb: Europe's leading Kate Bush tribute recreates the drama of Hounds of Love and beyond in Temple Bar.

events.title: CURVEBALL: 3Phoria Day Party
events.blurb: Early-evening bank-holiday day party from the CURVEBALL crew — dance music from 5pm so you're home before the babysitter clocks off.

events.title: WHEATS (Club Night)
events.blurb: Late-night bank-holiday club session at the Button Factory with house selector WHEATS.

events.title: When Chai Met Toast
events.blurb: Feel-good indie-folk from Kochi, India — When Chai Met Toast bring their sunny multilingual anthems to Dublin.

events.title: BassLine Dub: Sem Jacobs
events.blurb: Soundsystem culture in Temple Bar: BassLine Dub hosts Sem Jacobs for a late Saturday session.

events.title: POINTAKEN present Transmission (EP Release)
events.blurb: EP-release night on Wellington Quay as the Transmission tour hits The Workman's Club.

events.title: The Tommyguns
events.blurb: Dublin rock'n'roll four-piece The Tommyguns headline the Workman's live room on Saturday night.

events.title: DISORDER – Indie & Alternative Clubnight
events.blurb: Indie sleaze, post-punk and alternative anthems until late on the Workman's first floor — €5 in, no pretence.

events.title: No Scrubs: 90s & 00s R&B Party
events.blurb: TLC, Destiny's Child, Usher and every guilty pleasure in between — a Friday-night throwback R&B party.

events.title: Index D8 Afters: Fish56Octagon
events.blurb: Viral UK dance producer Fish56Octagon takes over the Academy for Index's late Friday session.

events.title: Lewis Taylor
events.blurb: Cult British soul auteur Lewis Taylor — beloved of D'Angelo fans — plays a rare late Dublin show on Abbey Street.

events.title: Thirteenth Step – A Perfect Circle Tribute
events.blurb: A Perfect Circle's catalogue played in full in the downstairs venue of Dublin's original rock bar, with support from Ritual Effect.

events.title: Sepultura Pre & After Show Party (Free)
events.blurb: All-day free party around Sepultura's farewell show: Slayer tribute Ghosts of War on the main stage, metal DJs downstairs, open on both floors from 11am.

events.title: Comedy Bang! Bang! Live
events.blurb: Scott Aukerman brings the beloved improv-podcast circus to Vicar Street for one night, bars open from 6:30pm.

events.title: David O'Doherty + Guests @ Craic Den Comedy Club
events.blurb: Keyboard-wielding Irish comedy hero David O'Doherty headlines the Craic Den's intimate cellar bill.

events.title: David O'Doherty + Guests @ Craic Den Comedy Club
events.blurb: Friday-night edition of the Craic Den with David O'Doherty topping a stacked club bill.

events.title: David O'Doherty + Guests @ Craic Den Comedy Club
events.blurb: Early Saturday show (7pm) from David O'Doherty and guests — a second 9:15pm sitting runs the same night.

events.title: Traditional Irish Musical Pub Crawl
events.blurb: Two professional musicians lead a moving concert through two historic bars, telling the story of Irish music with plenty of singalong. Nightly at 6pm except Saturdays; finishes on O'Connell Street by 8:15pm.

events.title: 1916 Rebellion Walking Tour
events.blurb: Historian Lorcan Collins' original Easter Rising tour, running since 1996 — GPO, Moore Street, City Hall and Dublin Castle in two brisk, brilliant hours. Daily at 11:30am (1pm Sundays).

events.title: Glasnevin Cemetery: Irish History Tour
events.blurb: Guided walk among the graves of Parnell, Collins, de Valera and 1.5 million other Dubliners, daily at 11:30am, 1:30pm and 2:30pm. The Gravediggers pub next door pours a famous pint afterwards.

events.title: Dublin Ghostbus Tour
events.blurb: Actor-storytellers pilot a sinister double-decker through Dublin's dark past — haunted graveyards, medieval torture demos and the ghosts of St Audoen's. Departures 7pm and 9:30pm on scheduled nights; book ahead.

events.title: Kilmainham Gaol Guided Tour
events.blurb: The former prison where the 1916 leaders were executed — the single most powerful history stop in Dublin. Guided tours daily 9am–5:15pm; summer slots sell out days ahead, so book online early.

events.title: Croke Park GAA Museum & Skyline Tour
events.blurb: Walk the roof of the 82,000-seat home of Gaelic games, 44 metres above the pitch, with the GAA Museum included. Daily tours (ages 12+ for the Skyline); schedules flex around match days.

events.title: Dalkey Castle Living History Tour
events.blurb: Costumed actors bring a genuine 14th-century townhouse castle to life in seaside Dalkey — archers, barber-surgeons and all. Great with kids, and the DART ride out along the bay is half the fun.

events.title: Howth Cliff Path Loop
events.blurb: The classic 6km clifftop loop from Howth DART station: gorse-covered headland, the Baily Lighthouse, seals in the harbour and fish and chips at the end. Doable with kids in about two hours.

events.title: Airfield Estate: Dublin's Working Farm
events.blurb: A 38-acre working farm and gardens in the suburbs — egg collecting at 10am, cow milking, donkeys at 3pm and adventure playgrounds. Open daily 9:30am–7:30pm in summer; farmers market Fridays and Saturdays.

events.title: Airfield Estate Summer Festival
events.blurb: Nine days of food, live music, craft workshops and family activities across the farm and gardens — the estate's big summer blowout starts during your last week.

events.title: Phoenix Park: Bikes, Deer & Victorian Tea Rooms
events.blurb: One of Europe's biggest enclosed city parks: rent bikes at the main gate, find the wild fallow deer herd, and picnic near Áras an Uachtaráin. Time Out's #3 thing to do in Dublin — free and endless with kids.

events.title: The Book of Kells Experience & Long Room
events.price: From €19; under-12s free on adult tickets
events.blurb: The 1,200-year-old manuscript plus the Long Room, where Luke Jerram's 7-metre glowing Earth 'Gaia' currently hangs among the shelves. Timed tickets online only — early-morning weekday slots are cheapest and quietest.

events.title: Little Museum of Dublin: The Green Mile Tour
events.blurb: A whistle-stop, guide-led romp through 20th-century Dublin in a Georgian townhouse on St Stephen's Green — freshly renovated, very funny, and doable in an hour. Daily 9:30am–5pm.

events.title: National Leprechaun Museum: Storytelling Tours
events.blurb: Live storytellers perform Irish folktales and myths on a 45-minute guided walk through giant-furniture rooms and optical-illusion tunnels. Tours every half hour, 10:30am–5:30pm; ages 6+.

events.title: Dublinia: Viking & Medieval Dublin
events.blurb: Hands-on Viking and medieval Dublin at Christchurch: try on chainmail, board a longship reconstruction and climb St Michael's Tower for the view. The most reliably kid-pleasing museum in town.

events.title: Guinness Storehouse & Gravity Bar
events.blurb: Seven storeys of stout history at St James's Gate, finishing with a pint (or a soft drink for the kids) in the 360° Gravity Bar. Open daily 9am–7pm; book a morning slot to dodge the crowds.

events.title: Marsh's Library
events.blurb: Ireland's oldest public library (1707), unchanged behind St Patrick's Cathedral — reading cages, Easter Rising bullet holes in the books, and a resident ghost. Tue–Sat only; closed Sundays and Mondays.

events.title: Chester Beatty: Manuscripts from Around the World
events.blurb: Free museum in the Dublin Castle gardens with one of the world's great collections of Islamic, East Asian and European manuscripts — plus a rooftop garden and a good café. A calm rainy-day ace.

events.title: MoLI – Museum of Literature Ireland
events.blurb: Joyce, Binchy and Rooney under one Georgian roof on St Stephen's Green, with 'Copy No. 1' of Ulysses and gorgeous hidden gardens out back. Daily 10:30am–5:30pm.

events.title: 14 Henrietta Street: Tenement Museum Tours
events.blurb: One Georgian townhouse, 300 years of Dublin life — from aristocratic splendour to tenement rooms that housed 100 people. Guided tours only; small groups, book ahead.

events.title: Shelbourne v St Patrick's Athletic (Dublin Derby)
events.blurb: Friday-night League of Ireland derby under the old floodlights of Tolka Park — Shels host St Pat's in one of Dublin football's proper fixtures.

events.title: BoyleSports Irish Greyhound Derby – Round 1
events.blurb: Opening round of greyhound racing's biggest Irish prize at Shelbourne Park, with live music after the last race — an only-in-Dublin Saturday night out.
